LESSON: READING ALOUD: POETRY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Reading 2.6 Guided Reading: Fluency (2 sessions) • Pace • Verbal cues By the end
Topic 2.8: Reading Aloud: Poetry

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading Aloud: Poetry. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we take care of our immediate environment?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a simple poem on weather for effective communication
2. apply non-verbal cues in presentation of a poem

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING ALOUD: POETRY
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading Aloud: Poetry helps you succeed in ARABIC LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING ALOUD: POETRY
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read a simple poem on weather for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to read a simple poem on weather for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a simple poem on weather for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Aloud: Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a simple poem on weather for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply non-verbal cues in presentation of a poem

What this means
In this part you learn to apply non-verbal cues in presentation of a poem. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply non-verbal cues in presentation of a poem.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading Aloud: Poetry to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply non-verbal cues in presentation of a poem. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading Aloud: Poetry is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading Aloud: Poetry”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read a simple poem on weather for effective communication)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading Aloud: Poetry to a partner. (skill: apply non-verbal cues in presentation of a poem)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading Aloud: Poetry to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read a simple poem on weather for effective communication.
3. Practise this skill: apply non-verbal cues in presentation of a poem.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading Aloud: Poetry from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading Aloud: Poetry: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Reading Aloud: Poetry?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we take care of our immediate environment?
2. Why are poems used in Arabic language?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading Aloud: Poetry means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read a simple poem on weather for effective communication.
5. Be able to: apply non-verbal cues in presentation of a poem.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
